title: Gaining time naturally
goal: Use natural French fillers and time-buying phrases (euh, bon, en fait, disons, comment dire, c'est-à-dire) to keep talking while you think, without sounding hesitant.

items.fr: euh / bon / en fait / disons / c'est-à-dire

drills.prompt: You need a second to think before answering a question in an interview. What sounds most natural?
options: C'est une bonne question… Disons que…
drills.explain: [[C'est une bonne question]] buys time politely, and [[Disons que…]] starts your answer while you think.

drills.text: Je travaille dans la santé, ___, je suis infirmière.
drills.en: I work in health care, that is, I'm a nurse.
drills.explain: [[c'est-à-dire (que)]] makes what you just said more precise.

drills.text: On pensait que c'était difficile. En ___, c'est très simple.
drills.en: We thought it was difficult. Actually, it's very simple.
drills.explain: [[En fait]] = actually, in fact. It often corrects an idea or adds precision.

items.note: A rounded vowel, like the e in le, held: euh… Not the English um.

accept: disons que

example.fr: J'habite ici depuis, disons, cinq ans.
example.en: I've lived here for, let's say, five years.

accept: Comment dirais-je…

items.en: that is, I mean, in other words
accept: c'est-à-dire que

items.note: Also means finally / at last. In speech, enfin often corrects: Il est grand, enfin, assez grand.

example.fr: C'est loin, enfin, pas trop loin.
example.en: It's far, well, not too far.

accept: Très bonne question.
Laisse-moi réfléchir…
Je réfléchis…
voyons voir

example.en: Let's see… it was a Tuesday.

accept: Je dirais…
J'ai oublié le mot.
Je ne trouve pas le mot.

steps.title: A real answer, with real hesitations
steps.intro: A community radio station in Sherbrooke is doing street interviews: *Qu'est-ce qui vous a surpris en arrivant au Québec ?* Listen to Amira's answer. She hesitates, but she **never stops talking**.

blocks.title: Micro-trottoir à Sherbrooke
blocks.context: A journalist stops Amira in the street.

lines.speaker: Journaliste
lines.fr: Bonjour madame ! Qu'est-ce qui vous a surprise en arrivant au Québec ?
lines.en: Hello, ma'am! What surprised you when you arrived in Québec?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oh… c'est une bonne question. Euh… bon, la première chose, c'est l'hiver, évidemment !
lines.en: Oh… that's a good question. Um… well, the first thing is winter, obviously!

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: En fait, ce n'est pas le froid qui m'a surprise. C'est… comment dire… la lumière. Il fait très beau, très clair, même à moins vingt.
lines.en: Actually, it's not the cold that surprised me. It's… how can I put it… the light. It's very sunny, very bright, even at minus twenty.

lines.speaker: Journaliste
lines.fr: Ah, intéressant ! Et à part l'hiver ?
lines.en: Oh, interesting! And apart from winter?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Voyons… je dirais que les gens sont très directs, enfin, directs mais gentils. C'est-à-dire qu'ils vous parlent facilement dans l'autobus ou à l'épicerie.
lines.en: Let's see… I'd say that people are very direct, well, direct but kind. I mean, they talk to you easily on the bus or at the grocery store.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Et puis, disons que j'ai dû apprendre un nouveau français ! Au début, quand on me disait « c'est le fun », je ne comprenais rien.
lines.en: And then, let's say I had to learn a new French! At first, when people told me “c'est le fun” (it's fun), I didn't understand a thing.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Maintenant, je le dis tout le temps ! Bon, voilà… merci à vous !
lines.en: Now I say it all the time! Well, there you go… thank you!

blocks.prompt: What does Amira do when she says “c'est une bonne question”?
blocks.explain: [[C'est une bonne question]] is a polite, natural way to gain a few seconds.

blocks.prompt: In “directs, enfin, directs mais gentils”, what does enfin mean?
blocks.explain: In speech, [[enfin]] often introduces a **self-correction**: she makes her idea more precise.

blocks.prompt: Why does Amira say “comment dire…” before “la lumière”?
options: She is searching for the right word
She is asking the journalist a question
blocks.explain: [[Comment dire…]] = *how can I put it…*: it fills the silence while you look for a word.

steps.title: Fill the silence the French way
steps.intro: Silence feels long when you speak a new language. Native speakers hesitate too, but they fill the gaps with **French** sounds and phrases. Using them makes you sound more fluent, not less.

blocks.title: Fillers and time-buyers by function
head: You want to…
Say…
Example
rows: Alors… euh… je suis arrivée en 2022.
C'est une bonne question. / Voyons… / Laissez-moi réfléchir…
Voyons… je dirais que c'est le logement.
Comment dire… / Le mot m'échappe… / C'est… le truc pour…
disons, je dirais que…, à peu près
J'habite ici depuis, disons, cinq ans.
Be more precise or correct yourself
en fait, c'est-à-dire (que), enfin, je veux dire
C'est loin, enfin, pas trop loin.
blocks.note: [[le truc]] (*the thing, the whatsit*) is informal but very useful when a noun escapes you: [[le truc pour ouvrir les bouteilles]] (a bottle opener).

blocks.title: How much is too much?
blocks.body:
Fillers are like salt: a little makes your French taste natural; too much ruins it.

- **One filler per idea** is plenty. [[Euh, bon, alors, en fait, disons…]] in one breath sounds lost.
- **Fill, then continue.** A filler must lead somewhere: [[Disons que…]] + your idea.
- **In an exam**, examiners accept natural hesitations. What lowers your score is long **silence**, English sounds (*um, like, you know*) and unfinished sentences.
- **If a word escapes you, talk around it:** [[C'est un endroit où on achète des médicaments]] = a pharmacy. This is called *paraphrase*, and it's a real skill.

blocks.title: Disons que / je dirais que
blocks.pattern: Disons que + phrase  /  Je dirais que + phrase
blocks.note: Both soften what follows and give you a second to think. [[Je dirais que]] uses the conditionnel of [[dire]] (B1 unit 6): *I would say that…*

examples.fr: Je dirais que le plus difficile, c'est la langue.
examples.en: I'd say that the hardest thing is the language.

blocks.title: Euh is not um
blocks.body:
English speakers hesitate with *um* or *uh*. French speakers hesitate on a **rounded vowel**, like the [[e]] of [[le]], held for a moment: [[euh…]] Round your lips as if you were going to say *oo*, but say *eh*.

Also:
- [[en fait]]: pronounce the final **t**: *an-fète*.
- [[c'est-à-dire]]: three quick syllables, *sé-ta-dir*.
- [[bon]]: a nasal vowel; don't pronounce the *n*.

blocks.title: Fillers you'll hear in Québec
blocks.body:
- [[ben]] (from *bien*): [[Ben oui !]] (*well, yes!*), [[Ben, je sais pas…]]. Very common everywhere in informal French.
- [[là]] at the end of a phrase, for emphasis: [[Je suis fatiguée, là.]]
- [[mettons]] = *let's say*, like [[disons]]: [[On se voit à 8 h, mettons ?]]
- [[genre]] = *like*, among young people: [[C'était genre super long.]]
- [[pis]] (from *puis*) = *and then*: [[pis après…]]

These are normal in Québec conversation. Understand them; in an exam or at work, prefer [[bon]], [[en fait]], [[disons]] and [[c'est-à-dire]].

blocks.title: Hesitation mistakes
blocks.body:
- **English fillers:** *um*, *like*, *you know*, *so* slip out under stress. Practise [[euh]], [[bon]] and [[en fait]] until they replace them.
- **Enfin = finally only:** in speech, [[enfin]] very often means *well, I mean*. [[Il est sympa, enfin… la plupart du temps.]]
- **Actuellement ≠ actually:** [[actuellement]] means *currently*. *Actually* = [[en fait]].
- **Je ne sais pas** as a filler: it sounds like you have no answer. Say [[C'est une bonne question…]] or [[Voyons…]] instead.
- **Apologizing all the time:** don't say [[Désolé, mon français…]] after every hesitation. Just continue.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Copy the **melody**: fillers are often said on a flat, slightly long tone, then the sentence starts again normally.

lines.fr: Euh… bon, la première chose, c'est l'hiver.
lines.en: Um… well, the first thing is winter.

lines.fr: En fait, ce n'est pas le froid qui m'a surprise.
lines.en: Actually, it's not the cold that surprised me.
It's… how can I put it… the light.

lines.fr: Voyons… je dirais que les gens sont très directs.
lines.en: Let's see… I'd say that people are very direct.
I mean, they talk to you easily.

lines.fr: C'est une bonne question. Laissez-moi réfléchir.
lines.en: That's a good question. Let me think.

blocks.fr: Mon travail ? Euh… disons que je suis dans l'informatique. En fait, je suis analyste de données.
blocks.en: My job? Um… let's say I'm in IT. Actually, I'm a data analyst.
blocks.prompt: What is the speaker's job, exactly?
blocks.explain: [[disons que]] gives a vague answer first; [[En fait]] then makes it precise: [[analyste de données]].

blocks.fr: J'ai besoin du… comment dire… du truc pour ouvrir les boîtes de conserve.
blocks.en: I need the… how can I put it… the thing for opening cans.
blocks.prompt: What object is the speaker looking for?
blocks.explain: The word escapes the speaker ([[un ouvre-boîte]]), so they describe it: [[le truc pour ouvrir les boîtes de conserve]].

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Choose the filler that fits the **function**: thinking, searching for a word, softening or making more precise.

blocks.prompt: Match each phrase with what the speaker is doing.
pairs: Il est grand, enfin, assez grand.

blocks.text: On dit que Québec est une petite ville. En ___, il y a plus de 500 000 habitants.
blocks.en: People say Québec City is a small city. Actually, there are more than 500,000 inhabitants.
blocks.explain: [[En fait]] corrects a common idea: *actually*. Careful: [[en effet]] (unit 9) confirms, it doesn't correct.

blocks.prompt: An interviewer asks you a question you didn't expect. What's the best start?
optionFeedback: This closes the conversation. Buy time instead.
English fillers: replace them with euh, bon, voyons.

blocks.prompt: I'd say that the hardest thing is the language.
accept: Je dirais que le plus difficile, c'est la langue.
Je dirais que le plus difficile est la langue.
Je dirais que la chose la plus difficile, c'est la langue.
Je dirais que la chose la plus difficile est la langue.
blocks.explain: [[Je dirais que…]] softens your answer. [[le plus difficile]] = the hardest thing (superlative).

blocks.text: Je travaille de nuit, ___, de 23 h à 7 h.
blocks.en: I work nights, that is, from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
blocks.explain: [[c'est-à-dire]] introduces a precise explanation of what you just said.

blocks.prompt: That's a good question, let me think.
accept: C'est une bonne question laissez-moi réfléchir
blocks.explain: Two time-buyers in a row: a compliment, then [[Laissez-moi réfléchir]] (imperative of [[laisser]] + [[moi]]).

blocks.prompt: In « Il est sympa, enfin… la plupart du temps », what does “enfin” do?
options: It corrects and limits what the speaker just said
blocks.explain: Spoken [[enfin]] = *well, I mean*: a self-correction. Context tells you which meaning it has.

blocks.prompt: I've lived here for, let's say, five years.
accept: J'habite ici depuis, disons, cinq ans.
J'habite ici depuis disons cinq ans.
Je vis ici depuis, disons, cinq ans.
J'habite ici depuis, disons, 5 ans.
Je vis ici depuis disons cinq ans.
blocks.explain: [[disons]] softens a number you're not sure about. Review (A2): [[depuis]] + present for something still true.

blocks.text: Si j'avais plus de temps, je ___ du bénévolat. (faire)
blocks.en: If I had more time, I would volunteer.
blocks.explain: Review (B1 unit 6): si + imparfait → conditionnel: [[je ferais]]. Interviewers love hypothetical questions!

blocks.fr: En fait, ce n'est pas le froid qui m'a surprise.
blocks.explain: [[En fait]] (actually) + [[c'est… qui]] to highlight. [[surprise]] agrees with [[m']] (a woman) because the object comes before [[avoir]].

blocks.prompt: Answer this street-interview question without preparing: “What surprised you most when you arrived in Canada (or in a new city)?” Speak for about 60 seconds. Use at least four different fillers or time-buyers, and never stay silent for more than two seconds.
checklist: Buy time at the start: C'est une bonne question… / Voyons…
A soft opinion: Je dirais que… / Disons que…
Search for a word aloud: Comment dire… (or paraphrase)
Make something more precise: en fait / c'est-à-dire
No English fillers, no long silences

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Oh, c'est une bonne question ! Voyons… je dirais que c'est la taille du pays. En fait, avant d'arriver, je pensais aller de Toronto à Montréal en une heure. Mais c'est, comment dire… c'est très loin ! C'est-à-dire qu'il faut cinq ou six heures en voiture. Et puis, disons que j'ai été surpris par la politesse des gens. Tout le monde s'excuse tout le temps, enfin, presque tout le monde. Bon, voilà, c'est ce qui m'a le plus surpris.
models.en: Oh, that's a good question! Let's see… I'd say it's the size of the country. Actually, before arriving, I thought I'd go from Toronto to Montréal in an hour. But it's, how can I put it… it's very far! I mean, you need five or six hours by car. And then, let's say I was surprised by how polite people are. Everyone apologizes all the time, well, almost everyone. So there you go, that's what surprised me most.

summary:
- Fill short silences with French sounds and words: [[euh]], [[bon]], [[alors]], [[voyons]]
- Buy time politely ([[C'est une bonne question]], [[Laissez-moi réfléchir]]), soften ([[disons]], [[je dirais que]]) and look for words ([[comment dire…]], or paraphrase)
- Make your idea precise with [[en fait]], [[c'est-à-dire]] and [[enfin]], one filler per idea, never English *um* or *like*

meta.notes: Removed 'm'a surpris' from the r10 dictation accepts (it sounds different from 'surprise'). Fixed 'c'est-à-dire: four syllables' → three, and added accept variants. Québec fillers (mettons, ben, pis, là) are correctly labelled informal.
